page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor. It features 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 210.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 98.02 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression also performs strongly at 31.99 GB/sec. However, CPU-bound tasks and multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall within the average range. Large language model text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the medium 7B model achieving a weak 7.8 tokens/sec and the small 135M model scoring a poor 40.51 tokens/sec.

Given its bare-metal architecture and massive 1.5 TB memory capacity, this server represents a high-resource-density tier. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring extreme memory footprints and high-speed network throughput without the need for local NVMe drives or GPU acceleration. The hardware profile is best suited for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, heavy data processing, and high-throughput network middleboxes.
